newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares dip, watch U.S. Greenspan response.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares dip, watch U.S. Greenspan response.

text.p: Danish share prices ended slightly lower on Wednesday, hit by a general dearth of investors and uncertainty regarding likely U.S. market response to Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Congressional testimony, which began after the Copenhagen bourse closed.
"The U.S. market reaction to Greenspan will determine the way Danish stock goes tomorrow, that is all one can say at this stage," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed a minimal 0.07 point lower at 154.53, while the KFX March future fell 0.70 point to 153.95 with 539 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Overall bourse turnover for the day was 1.08 billion crowns.
Although U.S. stocks intitially dipped on Greenspan's cautionary remarks analysts said that his stand on inflation was positive in the long-term.

On the Copenhagen bourse, Tele Danmark was the day's most traded paper, but fell a relatively modest three crowns to 348 on fears about draft legislation which it says compels it to give competitors cut-price access to its network.
A trades union official estimated that Tele Danmark could lose 1.2 billion crowns annually if the bill became law.
